items.title: cactus-compute/needle
items.contentSnippet:
14MB foundation model for tiny devices; phones, wearables, smart home, and robots.


 
Needle 2
 
Needle 2 is an open 45M-parameter model for tool calling, device use and structured extraction. The whole model is a single 14MB binary that runs a full session in about 28MB of RAM. It is built on our Simple Attention Network findings, compressed to CQ2-bit with Cactus Quants, and baked into its own engine. On the benchmarks below, Needle 2 trades wins with other small models like FunctionGemma 270

items.title: smicallef/spiderfoot
items.contentSnippet:
SpiderFoot automates OSINT for threat intelligence and mapping your attack surface.


 
       
 
SpiderFoot is an open source intelligence (OSINT) automation tool. It integrates with just about every data source available and utilises a range of methods for data analysis, making that data easy to navigate.
 
SpiderFoot has an embedded web-server for providing a clean and intuitive web-based interface but can also be used completely via the command-line. It's written in Python 3 and MIT-licensed

items.title: Show HN: Open-Source Framer Alternative
items.contentSnippet:
Hi,
I've been working for two years on a design-oriented website builder which i've just released.
Popular website builders like Framer and Webflow are great products, but their vendor-lock in and lack of proper code export is something that I found too non-user centric. You are paying rent on your own website.
So i've decided to create Revyme, which is open source, self-hostable where you can design and export your code in Next.JS to host it anywhere.

items.title: Show HN: Klisi – a GTK4/Adwaita callgrind profile viewer and generator
items.contentSnippet:
For a long time, I had been in search of a callgrind profile viewer that would better integrate with the GNOME desktop environment.
KCacheGrind is amazing, but I was looking for a GTK native alternative.
Recently, I took an interest in Clojure, so I decided to combine the two in one project.
The result of this is Klisi.
Try it out and let me know what you think.
You can read a small write-up about this first release on my blog[1].

items.contentSnippet:

Velorn is a GPLv3 desktop video editor for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It has a multi track video/audio timeline and works as a normal editor without any AI generation setup.
